title: Probing Latent Colombian Identity Inferences in Qwen2.5-7B with Natural Language Autoencoders

bias_targets.methodology: Using Natural Language Autoencoders (NLA) to verbalize residual-stream activations from prompts containing explicit, implicit, or neutral Colombian cues, and coding the resulting explanations for nationality mentions to detect latent national identity inferences.
Comparing the internal latent representations of matched prompts in Colombian Spanish versus English to identify cross-lingual divergences, geographic anchoring, and differential stereotyping.

Coding NLA-verbalized internal activations for socioeconomic status mentions, specifically examining how prompts about education or employment diverge contextually (e.g., local assistance vs. international mobility) based on language.
Analyzing the model's latent thoughts for homogenization or alteration of cultural references (e.g., gastronomy, local institutions) when processing implicit cues in different languages.
